dataset.description: The  data management plan is created to provide the framework for the data collection and generation to meet the goals of the research  project on career frameworks for the the regional growth in digital economy. It sets out the basic  research data management principles and outlines key resources and security measures.

distribution.title:
To reach the research goals the following data will be collected:

Demographic and socioeconomic data:
Employment trends (e.g., creation of new jobs, industry changes, professions in the digital economy).
Levels and distribution of digital skills across different population groups (e.g., by age, education, and profession).
Internet accessibility and infrastructure data in the Latgale region (e.g., broadband internet coverage).
Income and career development data related to the improvement of digital skills.
will be collected from the Central bureu of Statistics, the MInistry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development of the Republic of Latvia

Policy and regional data:
Impact indicators of National and regional policies in the context of digital transformation.
Regional Disparity Comparisons (e.g., Latgale compared to Riga or other regions in Latvia).
will be collected from the MInistry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development of the Republic of Latvia

Further in the research process the origin of the qualitative data will be defined, and it could be: 

Interviews: In-depth, structured interviews with stakeholders, including policymakers, business leaders, and representatives of educational institutions in the Latgale region.
Personal stories of successful transitions to work in the digital economy sectors.
or
Case Studies: documentation of successful projects (e.g., business promotion or skill enhancement initiatives).
or
Focus Groups: workshops or focus group discussions with regional participants to validate career development frameworks.

1.3. Secondary Data
Literature review: extracts from scientific articles, policy reviews, and databases on the digital economy, human capital, and regional employment disparities.
Comparative data: publicly available data from national and international sources (e.g., EU digital economy statistics, World Bank, OECD).

dmp.description:
The digital economy has become a critical driver of economic growth, innovation, and job creation globally. However, the benefits of this transformation are not evenly distributed, and many regions, particularly those outside major urban centers, face significant challenges in adapting to and capitalizing on digital advancements. The impact of AI-related industries on labor markets is significant, influencing both the quantity and structure of employment.
Regarding human capital and entrepreneurship, digital finance development significantly boosts urban entrepreneurial activity, with advanced human capital structures positively moderating this process. Human capital plays a crucial role in the development of high-tech industries and the digital economy, as ongoing digitalization significantly impacts its formation and development.
This postdoctoral research aims to explore and identify effective career development frameworks for individuals in these regions to enhance employment opportunities in the era digital economy, identifying the necessary infrastructure and human capital development policy adjustments to improve the work and life standards and foster the economy growth in the region.
dmp.title: Career development frameworks to boost regional development in the era of digital economy
